question: After rebasing onto current main, should terminal-test reliability be owned by this ten-second wait budget, the retained-module isolation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105711, or a deliberately tested combination?
rationale: Both approaches are technically plausible, but current main removed the original need to couple them and repository evidence cannot determine whether the timeout remains necessary after structural isolation without maintainer intent and combined exact-head proof.

options.title: Prefer structural isolation
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105711 as the canonical terminal fix and retain the wider waits only if post-isolation stress runs still reproduce genuine scheduler starvation.

options.title: Keep bounded waits
options.body: Land this PR’s timeout approach and close the structural isolation path only if the retained-module diagnosis is disproven by exact-head evidence.

options.title: Prove both mechanisms
options.body: Combine isolation and the wait budget only with refreshed stress evidence showing that each protects a distinct observed failure mode.

recommendation.title: Prefer structural isolation
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105711 as the canonical terminal fix and retain the wider waits only if post-isolation stress runs still reproduce genuine scheduler starvation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent authored this combined branch, its terminal-only subset, and the current-main CI change that removed the original coupling premise.
